citation: Polydefkis M, Arezzo J, Nash M, Bril V, Shaibani A, Gordon RJ, Bradshaw KL, Junor RWJ; Ranirestat Study Group. Safety and efficacy of ranirestat in patients with mild-to-moderate diabetic sensorimotor polyneuropathy. J Peripher Nerv Syst 2015;20(4):363–371
text_quality: partial: publisher PDF with a text layer, 9 pages, main text, tables 1–3, figures 1–2 and investigator appendix complete. The online-only Supporting Information (Appendix S1, Table S1, Figure S1, which list every secondary and exploratory measure) is not in the PDF. Page numbers are PDF pages (PDF 1–9 = journal pages 363–371).
design: Global, multicentre (84 sites), randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, three-arm parallel phase II/III trial (NCT00927914), 1:1:1, IVRS allocation stratified by site; 1-month run-in, 24 months of treatment, 1-month follow-up. Analysis by ANCOVA with LOCF and Dunnett adjustment; the combined-dose comparison was post hoc.
population: Adults 18–75 with type 1 or type 2 diabetes for at least 12 months (stable glycaemic control at least 3 months) and symptomatic diabetic sensorimotor polyneuropathy by AAN criteria with abnormal peroneal motor conduction velocity. Excluded: foot ulcer or amputation, non-diabetic neuropathy causes, hypothyroidism, B12/folate deficiency and others. Mean age about 57.6, 88% type 2, mean HbA1c about 7.9%, DSPN duration about 4.5 years.
n: 800 randomised: placebo 265, ranirestat 40 mg 264, 80 mg 271 (2,721 screened); 785 in the safety population; 633 (79%) completed.
setting: 84 sites in Asia, Europe, North America and Russia; July 2009 to January 2013; sponsor Eisai.
intervention: Oral ranirestat (AS-3201), an aldose reductase inhibitor, 40 mg/day or 80 mg/day for 24 months.
duration: 24 months of treatment (mean exposure about 21–22 months).
outcomes: Primary: change in peroneal motor nerve conduction velocity (PMNCV) at 24 months, target difference of at least 1.2 m/s. Secondary: NTSS-6-SA symptom score, vibration perception threshold. Exploratory (Supporting Information): signs and symptoms, sensory capacity, quality of life, pain, other electrophysiology. No skin biopsy or other small-fibre measure.

key_results.quote: Incorporating a dedicated measure of small caliber fiber such as skin biopsy was considered although ultimately not used due to the fact that regulatory authorities did not accept a change in this measure as a criterion for approval.

Secondary and exploratory measures including signs and symptoms of DSPN, sensory capacity, quality of life, pain, and various electrophysiological parameters did not show a trend toward treatment effect
The mean improvement from baseline at 24 months was +0.49, +0.95, and +0.90 m/s for placebo, ranirestat 40 mg and 80 mg, respectively (NS).
The treatment difference vs. placebo reached significance when ranirestat groups were combined in a post hoc analysis (+0.44 m/s; p = 0.0237).
Unexpectedly, PMNCV improved rather than declined … over time in the placebo group (+0.49 m/s at 24 months).
Ranirestat was well tolerated and improved PMNCV vs. placebo, but not to the 1.2 m/s threshold.

author_limitations.quote: The lack of progression in the placebo group contributed to ranirestat not meeting the primary endpoint goal of a 1.2 m/s improvement in PMNCV.
Dropouts over time and the LOCF approach may have underestimated efficacy measures in this study.
Future studies should include additional measures of small fiber structure or function such as skin biopsy and more contemporary longitudinal data are needed using these measures.

funding_conflicts: Funded by Eisai; editorial support funded by Eisai Ltd. Two authors (R.J.G., K.L.B.) were full-time Eisai employees, the guarantor among them; J.A. received an Eisai grant to set up and review the NCV data; V.B. is a consultant for Eisai and others. M.P., A.Z., M.N. and R.W.J.J. declare nothing to disclose.

studies_it_cites_that_matter.why: Earlier ranirestat RCT with sural nerve biopsies for nerve sorbitol and fructose, not skin; bears on the ARI class pages but not on A027 (skin) or A026 (epalrestat).

studies_it_cites_that_matter.citation: Gibbons CH, Freeman R, Tecilazich F, et al. The evolving natural history of neurophysiologic function in patients with well-controlled diabetes. J Peripher Nerv Syst 2013;18:153–161
studies_it_cites_that_matter.why: In well-controlled diabetes nerve conduction stayed stable over 3 years while small-fibre function worsened; context for placebo arms that do not progress (the trial's failure mode).
